q:
Match the CPU registers with their roles:
1. PC   2. IR   3. MAR   4. MDR
P. Holds the address of the memory location to be accessed
Q. Holds the data being transferred to/from memory
R. Holds the instruction currently being executed
S. Holds the address of the next instruction
exp: PC holds the next instruction address, IR the current instruction, MAR the memory address and MDR the data word.

q: A single even-parity bit appended to a data word fails to detect
options: two bits flipping in the word
a stuck-at-1 error on one bit
exp: Two flips keep the number of 1s even, so the parity check passes; a single parity bit detects only an odd number of errors.

q: Main memory is 64 KB and the cache is 1 KB with 16-byte blocks, direct mapped. How many tag bits are in each cache line's tag?
exp: Address = 16 bits; offset = 4 bits; lines = 1024/16 = 64, so index = 6 bits; tag = 16 - 4 - 6 = 6 bits.

q: Which of the following is NOT a technique for reducing the penalty of control (branch) hazards?
exp: Operand forwarding resolves data hazards; the other three deal with branches.

q:
Assertion (A): DMA improves system performance for bulk data transfers.
Reason (R): A DMA controller moves data between an I/O device and memory without the CPU executing instructions for each word.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
exp: Because the CPU is not involved word by word, it is free for other work, which is why DMA is efficient for bulk transfers.

q: The Intel 4004, the first commercial microprocessor, is associated with which generation of computers?
exp: Microprocessors built with LSI/VLSI technology mark the fourth generation.

q: In 8-bit two's complement arithmetic, adding +100 and +50 gives
exp: 01100100 + 00110010 = 10010110, which is -106 in two's complement; two positives giving a negative means overflow.

q: The 8-bit register 10110100 undergoes an arithmetic shift right by one position. The new content is
exp: An arithmetic shift right keeps the sign bit and copies it into the vacated position: 1 1011010. The logical shift would give 01011010.

q: A fully associative cache with 3 lines uses LRU replacement and is initially empty. Block references arrive in the order 1, 2, 3, 1, 4, 2. The number of misses is
exp: 1 M, 2 M, 3 M, 1 H, 4 M (evicts 2), 2 M (evicts 3): total 5 misses.

q: Which of the following is a CISC architecture?
exp: x86 has variable-length, complex instructions; ARM, MIPS and SPARC are RISC designs.

q: In a vectored interrupt system, the interrupting device supplies
options: The opcode of the next instruction
An address or index that identifies its service routine
exp: The vector lets the CPU jump directly to the correct interrupt service routine without polling devices.

q: Which statement correctly compares SRAM and DRAM?
options: SRAM needs refresh and is cheaper per bit than DRAM
DRAM is faster than SRAM and is used for cache
Both need refreshing but SRAM has lower density
SRAM uses a flip-flop cell and needs no refresh; DRAM uses a transistor-capacitor cell and needs refresh
exp: SRAM (6 transistors) is fast and used for cache; DRAM (1 transistor + 1 capacitor) is denser and cheaper, used as main memory, but needs refresh.

q: Which statement about horizontal microinstructions is correct?
options: They require extensive decoding of encoded fields
They have shorter control words than vertical microinstructions
They allow many micro-operations in parallel with little decoding
They can specify only one micro-operation at a time
exp: Horizontal microcode has long words with one bit per control signal, giving high parallelism and minimal decoding.

q: On a single-accumulator (one-address) machine, the minimum number of instructions needed to compute X = (A + B) * C is
exp: LOAD A, ADD B, MUL C, STORE X: four instructions.

q: How many 1K × 8 RAM chips are required to build a memory of 8K × 16?
exp: 8K/1K = 8 chips along the depth and 16/8 = 2 along the width: 8 × 2 = 16 chips.

q: A 4-stage pipeline has stage delays of 20, 30, 25 and 35 ns, and each pipeline register adds 5 ns. The time taken to execute 10 instructions is
exp: Clock = 35 + 5 = 40 ns; cycles = 4 + 9 = 13; time = 13 × 40 = 520 ns.

q:
Match the I/O technique with its description:
1. Programmed I/O   2. Interrupt-driven I/O   3. DMA
P. CPU continuously tests device status
Q. Device signals the CPU when it is ready
R. Controller moves a block directly between device and memory
exp: Programmed I/O polls, interrupt-driven I/O waits for a device signal, DMA transfers blocks without CPU intervention.

q: A multicore processor in which each core executes its own instruction stream on its own data is classified in Flynn's taxonomy as
exp: Multiple independent instruction streams operating on multiple data streams is MIMD.

q: A system uses 32-bit virtual addresses and 4 KB pages. The number of pages in the virtual address space is
exp: Page offset = 12 bits, so the page number has 32 - 12 = 20 bits, giving 2²⁰ pages.

q: Booth's algorithm is used in an ALU for
options: multiplication of signed numbers in 2's complement form
conversion of binary numbers to BCD
exp: Booth's algorithm multiplies signed 2's complement numbers by examining bit pairs of the multiplier and skipping runs of 1s.

q: Which bus carries the signals that indicate whether a memory operation is a read or a write?
exp: Read/write, clock and interrupt signals travel on the control bus.

q: Adding one overall parity bit to a Hamming single-error-correcting code (SEC-DED) makes it able to
options: correct single-bit errors and detect double-bit errors
correct burst errors of any length
exp: Extended Hamming code has minimum distance 4: it corrects one error and detects two, as used in ECC memory.

q: A two-level cache: L1 hit rate 90% with 2 ns access; L2 local hit rate 80% with 10 ns access; main memory 100 ns. The average memory access time is

A classic 5-stage pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) has no forwarding. The register file is written in the first half and read in the second half of a cycle. An instruction immediately followed by one that uses its result needs how many stall cycles?
exp: The dependent instruction can read the register only in the cycle the producer is in WB, which is 2 cycles later than normal ID.

q: When a maskable interrupt is recognised by a CPU with interrupts enabled, the processor first
options: Stops immediately in the middle of the current instruction
Resets the program counter to zero
exp: Interrupts are checked at instruction boundaries; the current instruction finishes before the PC and state are saved.

q: A disk has 4 platters (both surfaces used), 1000 tracks per surface, 100 sectors per track and 512 bytes per sector. Taking 1 MB = 10⁶ bytes, its capacity is approximately
In the IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point format, how many bits are used for the exponent?
exp: Single precision has 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits and 23 fraction bits.

q: In the MIPS architecture, an instruction such as add $t0, $t1, $t2 belongs to which instruction format?
exp: Register-register arithmetic instructions use the R-type format.

q: In a content-addressable (associative) memory, a word is located by
exp: CAM compares the search key with all stored words in parallel and returns matching locations.

q: Register windows, used to speed up procedure calls, are a feature of
exp: RISC designs like SPARC overlap sets of registers to avoid saving and restoring them on calls.

q: A device transfers 2000 bytes to memory by DMA in burst mode. The bus is 4 bytes wide and each memory cycle takes 200 ns. For how long is the bus held by the DMA controller?
CRC (cyclic redundancy check) detects errors by
options: adding all the data words and sending the sum
counting the number of 1s in each word
dividing the data by a generator polynomial using modulo-2 arithmetic and appending the remainder
transmitting every word twice and comparing
exp: The sender appends the remainder of the modulo-2 division; the receiver's division of the whole frame must leave remainder 0. CRC catches burst errors.

q: A processor has a byte-addressable memory and fixed 32-bit instructions. If the PC is 0x1000, what is its value after three sequential instructions have been fetched?
exp: Each instruction is 4 bytes, so PC = 0x1000 + 12 = 0x100C.

q:
Assertion (A): Base register addressing helps in program relocation.
Reason (R): Changing the contents of the base register shifts all the effective addresses without modifying the address fields in the instructions.
options: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
exp: EA = base + displacement, so loading a new base relocates the program without editing instructions.

q: A cache is 8 KB, 2-way set associative, with 32-byte blocks. The number of sets is
In a pipeline, 20% of instructions are branches and each branch causes 2 stall cycles. Ignoring other stalls, the average CPI is
Which of the following interrupts is normally given the highest priority?
exp: A power-failure interrupt must be handled immediately to save the machine state, so it ranks highest.

q: In a DRAM chip, the RAS and CAS signals are used to
options: enable the data bus drivers only
latch the row address and the column address in turn on shared address pins
exp: DRAM multiplexes the address: RAS latches the row address, then CAS latches the column address, halving the number of address pins.

q: A 3-frame memory uses FIFO page replacement and starts empty. For the reference string 2, 3, 2, 1, 5, 2, 4, 5, 3, 2, 5, 2 the number of page faults is
exp: Faults occur on 2,3,1,5,2,4,3,5,2 (hits on the repeated 2, 5 and 2 at positions 3, 8 and 10), giving 9 faults.

q: In an ALU, which status flag indicates an unsigned overflow (carry out of the MSB) after an addition?
exp: The carry flag is set when the addition produces a carry out of the most significant bit; the V flag is for signed overflow.
